message.content:
**Typical offset:**  
Berlin is normally **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.

**Why it can change:**  
Both cities observe daylight‑saving time, but their start/end dates differ:

| Period | Los Angeles (UTC‑8/PDT) | Berlin (UTC+1/CEST) | Offset |
|--------|------------------------|---------------------|--------|
| Early March – 14 Mar | PST (UTC‑8) | CET (UTC+1) | **9 h** |
| 14 Mar – 31 Mar | PST (UTC‑8) | CEST (UTC+2) | **10 h** |
| 31 Mar – 5 Nov | PDT (UTC‑7) | CEST (UTC+2) | **9 h** |
| 5 Nov – 31 Oct | PDT (UTC‑7) | CET (UTC+1) | **8 h** |
| After 5 Nov | PST (UTC‑8) | CET (UTC+1) | **9 h** |

So, while the usual difference is 9 hours, there are short windows (late March–early April and late October–early November) when the offset shifts to 10 or 8 hours.
